card.name: Bollywood
card.era: Emerged early 20th century with Hindi cinema; term coined 1970s
card.tagline: Film-derived Indian fusion dance blending classical, folk and Western styles
card.profile: Bollywood dance is the popular film-derived dance style of Hindi cinema, a synthesis of Indian classical (Kathak, Bharatanatyam) and folk traditions (bhangra, garba) fused with Western forms such as jazz, disco and hip-hop (Wikipedia). It evolved with the rise of Indian cinema in the early 20th century; the term 'Bollywood' (Bombay + Hollywood) was coined in the 1970s when the conventions of commercial masala Hindi films were established, with Yaadon Ki Baarat (1973) cited as the first quintessentially Bollywood film (Wikipedia). Group choreography, expressive facial gestures and synchronization to playback songs make it a global cultural phenomenon.
card.insight: Performers such as Helen, often called Bollywood's first 'item girl', helped blend Western cabaret and disco with Indian elements, and Hindi dance music reached global audiences through tracks such as 'Jai Ho', which won the Academy Award for Best Original Song on 22 February 2009 (Wikipedia).
